snippet.title: 【それでもヒグマに襲われた、、】動物を知り尽くしたベテラン写真家・星野道夫が命を落としてしまった1996年カムチャッカ事件の真実とは…
snippet.description:
1996年、ロシア・カムチャッカ。
「クマと心は通じる」と信じ、生涯銃を持たなかった写真家・星野道夫。
その命を奪ったのは、人間が変えてしまった一頭のヒグマでした。

アラスカの原野を18年撮り続け『旅をする木』で知られた世界的写真家は、なぜ"餌付け"されたヒグマに襲われたのか。クリル湖で起きた事件の経緯、額に赤い傷を持つ加害個体の正体、そして10年後に判明した「Food Conditioned（食物条件付け）」の恐ろしさを、地形図とアニメーションで解説します。

0:00 導入

1:36 銃を持たないという哲学
2:06 カムチャッカ、6名の撮影チーム
3:26 深夜の警告 ―赤い傷のヒグマ
5:03 「サケがあるから襲わない」という確信
7:49 8月8日、午前4時 ―そして「最後の写真」の真実
10:18 餌付けが生んだ加害個体 ―Food Conditioned
13:45 報告書の矛盾と、心ない非難

19:57 7年後の、もうひとつの悲劇
21:16 『旅をする木』 ―遺された言葉と家族

en-US.title: [Still Attacked by a Brown Bear...] The Truth Behind the 1996 Kamchatka Incident That Claimed the...
en-US.description:
1996, Kamchatka, Russia.

Photographer Michio Hoshino, who believed he could communicate with bears and never carried a gun in his life,

his life was taken by a brown bear whose behavior had been altered by humans.

Why was this world-renowned photographer, known for his 18 years of photographing the Alaskan wilderness and his work "The Traveling Tree," attacked by a brown bear that had been "food-conditioned"? This documentary explains the events of the incident at Kuril Lake, the identity of the attacking bear with a red scar on its forehead, and the terrifying reality of "food conditioning" that became apparent 10 years later, using topographic maps and animation.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Table of Contents
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
0:00 Introduction
0:27 To Alaska - A 19-Year-Old's Solo Journey
1:36 The Philosophy of Not Carrying a Gun
2:06 Kamchatka, a 6-Person Film Crew
3:26 A Warning in the Middle of the Night - The Brown Bear with a Red Scar
5:03 The Conviction That "It Won't Attack Because There Are Salmon"
7:49 August 8th, 4 AM - And the Truth Behind the "Last Photograph"
10:18 The Aggressor Created by Feeding - Food Conditioned
13:45 Contradictions in the Report and Heartless Accusations
17:10 The Truth 10 Years Later and "Earth Symphony No. 3"
18:27 Lake Kuril Changed by the Incident - Lebenko's Records
19:57 Another Tragedy 7 Years Later
21:16 "The Traveling Tree" —Words Left Behind and Family

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
References
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
• Yosuke Kosaka & Takuya Oyama, "Michio Hoshino: Eternal Gaze," Yama-kei Publishers, 2006
• Michio Hoshino, "The Traveling Tree," Bungei Shunju, 1994
• PRESIDENT Online, "The Terror of Bears That Have Become Tame" https://president.jp/articles/-/106990
• Wikipedia, "Michio Hoshino" https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/星野道夫

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

There is absolutely no intention to disrespect the accident, the deceased, or their family.

We hope that this incident will provide an opportunity for each individual to consider how they interact with nature.
